messages.subject: Help with logistic regression with genotypes
messages.subject_clean: Help with logistic regression with genotypes
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone!

I'm a relatively new user to R. I've used SAS and SPSS in the past and
I'm a perl coder at heart so I thought I'd give R a try given how it
can be scripted more easily (plus it's open source and I love that).

Anyway I'm doing genetics research and I'm trying to set up a
relatively simple logistic regression with disease as the outcome and
a SNP genotype as a predictor. I've coded the disease as 0 and 1 and
the genotype as 0, 1, 2 where 0 is the homozygote wildtype and 1 is
the heterzygote and 2 is the homozygote variant.

I would like to know the 95% CI for the odds ratio for the SNP
genotype coded as 1 and 2 (obviously 0 would be the reference group).

Any help getting R to display this data? I've tried using the builtin
glm command:

glm(AMD ~ rs10020202, family = binomial)

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Error in loading deSolve
messages.body_plain:
Time to contact the maintainer of the deSolve package.  If it is
compiled from sources and it doesn't load then that's a bug.  They
might be making assumptions about the form of names generated by the
Fortran compiler or something like that but, in any case, it is not a
clean compile if that symbol is referenced and not defined.

I have cc:d the maintainer on this reply.

1) Open MS.Excel
2) File -> Open  then select your file
3) in file type select All Files Then Select your file
4) in Import Dialog Box That appear Select Deliminated Radio Button
select NEXT
5)Select Deliminator == Space and Treat consecutive deliminater
6) select Finish
7)if alla thing seems Right  in MS Excel goto Data Filter Auto Filter
8) Go to Column  "Call" and Select "AAA"
9 Copy all items and paste in a new Worksheet
